end.summary:
Ordered human levels several times: cell → tissue → organ → organ system → organism; order was partly practised and needs checking again.
Gave partly correct human and plant examples, including muscle tissue, stomach, digestive system, leaf, xylem and shoot system; examples need further checking.
Discussed how organs in a system depend on one another; this was partly practised and needs another check.
The organ–organ system distinction was discussed, but the mix-up was not confirmed corrected after the last seen instance.
end.parentNote: Asha practised ordering levels of organisation, matching examples in humans and plants, and linking the parts of a system. Yash used several relevant examples and discussed how the stomach, intestines and liver work together. The difference between an organ and an organ system, and how much of a system can continue if one part stops, still needs checking. At home, ask Yash to make two five-step chains—one human and one plant—and say one example and one dependency at each step.

nahi... liver apna kaam karega toh digestive system ka woh part toh chal raha hai, lekin khaana toh system ke through jaata hai na, toh agar pet band hai toh aage ka rasta ruk gaya... toh half system chal raha hai half nahi?

Haan, aapka matlab sahi hai: pet se khaana aage na jaaye toh intestines ka kaam rukega, par liver jaise doosre hisse kaam kar sakte hain. Isliye poore system ko 'half chal raha hai' kehne ke bajay, uska kuch kaam prabhavit hai kehna zyada theek hai. Board ki seedhi mein organ ke theek baad kaunsa level aata hai?
